neighbours.label: A physical quantity (mass, weight, volume, force, gravity) described as absent or zero in a physics setting (weightlessness, zero volume, massless), vs the same quantity present and nonzero
fire: In this model each atom is treated as a point of zero size that moves freely.
Inside the orbiting station the crew float in weightlessness for months.
A photon is a particle of zero rest mass that always moves at light speed.
For the exercise, assume the pulley is massless and the rope has no weight.
Students imagine a frictionless plane on which the block slides of zero resistance.
During free fall the passengers briefly experience weightlessness in the plane.
The ideal spring here is taken to be of negligible mass compared with the block.
Treat the charged sphere as a point charge of zero radius at the origin.
quiet: In this model each atom is treated as a sphere of fixed size that bounces around.
Inside the orbiting station the crew exercise daily to keep their bones strong.
A proton is a particle with a large rest mass compared with the electron.
For the exercise, assume the pulley is heavy and the rope is quite long.
Students measured how far the block slid down the wooden ramp each time.
During the flight the passengers ate a small meal and watched a movie.
The heavy spring here stretches several centimeters when the block is added.
Treat the charged sphere as a metal ball of about two centimeters across.

predictions: Fire items 0.2-0.7 on 'of' or the quantity word; near misses under 0.15.
notes: Card peaks: 'Weightlessness', 'particles of zero volume', Japanese 反重力 (anti-gravity), 費用 in 'no cost at all', 'irrespective of the load'. Probe: 'particles of zero volume' 0.715 (on ' of'), 'simulate weightlessness' 0.357; plain force on a car 0.174, torque 0.088, load on beams 0.043, figurative weight 0.108. The absence reading is a guess the probe only partly supports.
